representation_fit.evidence: Designed representation matches the brief's workflow shape precisely: a single sequential release flow of 4 stages / 10 steps with irreversible gates and a recovery window (source/app.js:21-59); brief suggests object_type=workflow with recovery/confirm on irreversible steps. Deduction: the workflow is never presented on screen — both screenshots (1280x860, 1440x900) show an empty left nav, empty center panel, and no flow at all, so the delivered representation is only verifiable in code.

primary_task_salience.evidence: The goal is asserted prominently in the header — 「目标：零失误走完全程 — 不可逆步骤均有确认与恢复路径」 (source/index.html:16, visible top of both screenshots) and echoed in the log (00:00 entry). But the task itself is absent from the initial screen: #nav and #panel render nothing (screenshots), so there is no step, gate, or primary action dominating the screen — the dominant visual is empty space.

time_to_understand.evidence: What: brand, product/version (checkout-api v2.14.0), and success criterion are readable within seconds via header and legend (index.html:11-32; both screenshots). Where: unanswerable — no stage buttons, no step cards, no controls render (1280x860.png center/left columns empty), so a user cannot see where to act after reading the header.

navigation_cost.evidence: As rendered, the primary object is unreachable: the stage nav (#nav, index.html:26) and main panel (#panel, index.html:35) are empty in both viewports. Root cause in source: FLOW.stages.filter(stageComplete) at app.js:143 passes a stage object into stageComplete(id) whose stageById lookup (app.js:89-92) then returns undefined → TypeError inside renderChips, the first call of renderAll() (app.js:479-480, invoked at app.js:630), so renderNav/renderPanel never execute. Intended design was zero-navigation single-page (index.html:24-41); delivered cost is maximal.

context_loss.evidence: Source structure is strongly context-preserving: persistent three-pane single page (index.html:23-41), stage switching via in-place render with no route change (app.js:488-497), forced-confirm modals with cancel that return to the same state (app.js:404-424), follow-mode with 「回到当前阶段」 recovery button (app.js:327-328). Deduction: unverifiable at runtime because no interactive surface ever renders.

ui_surface_complexity.evidence: Designed permanent surfaces are proportionate to need — stage nav, flowstrip, status chips, log, banner (app.js:142-184, 303-309; index.html:19-40) for a 10-step flow, no clutter. But the delivered surface is missing nearly all needed controls: only header, legend card, and log render (both screenshots), which is inadequacy rather than simplicity.

accessibility.evidence: Receipt provides zero a11y verification: a11y.contrast, a11y.focus_order, a11y.target_size all skipped with target_invalid=true (measurement-summary.json:13-18). Visible affordance evidence: the rendered page exposes no operable controls at all (screenshots). Source shows some good semantics — lang=zh-CN (index.html:2), aria-live on panel (index.html:35), labeled checkboxes (app.js:239-240), noscript fallback (index.html:47) — but also 10-12px low-contrast grays for hints/legend/timestamps (styles.css:67,125,147,181,213) that went unmeasured.

frontend_rework.evidence: Fatal visible defect identical at both viewports: the app shell renders (header, legend, log) but #chips, #nav, #panel and the progress fill stay permanently empty due to the initial-render crash at app.js:143 (TypeError in renderChips, first call of renderAll at app.js:479-630; only the pre-render bootLog entries appear, app.js:624-630). Receipt corroborates: target_invalid=true, pass 0 / fail 0 / skipped 7 (measurement-summary.json:3-18) — checks could not run.

acceptance_seed_coverage.evidence: Seed 「不可逆步骤有恢复/确认路径」 is comprehensively addressed in source: full-rollout (c2) requires a modal with 3 consequence checkboxes plus typed confirmation code ROLLOUT-PROD (app.js:339-358); window-seal (d2) likewise with code SEAL (app.js:381-398); rollback recovery stays available until seal and is explicitly not counted as a mistake (app.js:177-181, 363-379); out-of-order attempts are guarded with recorded mistakes (app.js:565, 575); legend states the promise (index.html:28-29). No UI-level evidence because none of it renders (screenshots).

defects_observed: Initial-render crash: FLOW.stages.filter(stageComplete) (source/app.js:143) passes a stage object to stageComplete(id); stageById returns undefined and .steps throws (app.js:89-92), aborting renderAll() (app.js:479-480) before renderNav/renderPanel — #chips, #nav, #panel never populate, visible as an empty left column and center panel in both screenshots
Primary workflow object (4 stages / 10 steps) entirely absent from the initial screen at 1280x860 and 1440x900; only a type legend and a boot log render
Measurement receipt invalid: target_invalid=true with all seven checks skipped, 0 pass / 0 fail (measurement-summary.json:3-18)
Small low-contrast gray text used for hints, legend note, and log timestamps (source/styles.css:67,125,147,181,213) — flagged as risk only, since receipt contrast check was skipped
missing_evidence: No receipt measurement evidence: all 7 checks skipped due to target_invalid=true (measurement-summary.json:10-18), so layout overflow, responsive collision, truncation, contrast, focus order, and target size are unmeasured
Any interactive or post-initial state (confirm modals, rollback banner, completion certificate) is unverifiable at runtime because the initial render crashes before any control appears
scores.overall_note: This package pairs a conceptually excellent design with a fatal delivery defect. The source (source/app.js:12-59, 336-400) implements exactly the briefed representation — a single high-consequence release workflow with sequenced stages, forced-confirmation modals with typed codes on both irreversible steps, and a rollback recovery path open until seal, directly covering the acceptance seed. But the initial render crashes: FLOW.stages.filter(stageComplete) at app.js:143 passes a stage object where an id string is expected, throwing inside renderChips (the first call of renderAll, app.js:479-630), so the status chips, stage nav, and the entire center panel never render. Both operator screenshots confirm the result: a header, a legend card, and a log, with the workflow itself invisible and no actionable control anywhere on screen. The sanitized receipt agrees that the target was invalid with all seven checks skipped (measurement-summary.json:3-18). Navigation cost, task salience, and rework therefore score at the bottom despite strong source-level design; these scores reflect the delivered, observable product, and model-based judgment here is not a substitute for human preference.
